ratings.reviewer_notes: Directly links AF-associated atrial fibrosis to FMOD-regulated TLR4/MyD88/NLRP3 inflammasome signaling, caspase-1/IL-1β activation, and downstream TGF-β1/Smad signaling.
Provides experimental and clinical evidence that IL-6 activates atrial pSTAT3/STAT3 signaling, elicits early profibrotic changes, and increases susceptibility to postoperative AF.
Direct intervention study showing that TLR4 silencing suppresses the NLRP3–TGF-β pathway, fibroblast proliferation, collagen expression, atrial fibrosis, and AF susceptibility.

Relevant review of NLRP3 inflammatory signaling in AF across cardiomyocytes, myofibroblasts, and immune cells, but the abstract does not explicitly detail the inflammasome-to-atrial-fibrosis mechanism.
Directly shows that BMP2 reduces atrial fibrosis and AF susceptibility by inhibiting fibroblast NLRP3/ASC/caspase-1 inflammasome signaling and IL-1β/IL-6 production.
Focused review of inflammation–fibrosis interactions in AF, explicitly identifying RAAS, TGF-β/Smad, TNF-α/NF-κB, and IL-6/STAT3 pathways.
Offers broader cardiovascular-aging context for inflammatory and fibrotic pathways including NF-κB, NLRP3, IL-6, RAAS, and TGF-β; AF is only one of several diseases considered.
Direct causal evidence that fibroblast-restricted NLRP3 inflammasome activation induces proarrhythmic atrial fibrosis, slowed conduction, and an AF-promoting substrate.
Human atrial biopsy evidence associates AF severity with TGF-β1, fibroblast abundance, and collagen V, supporting a profibrotic pathway but not directly testing an inflammatory mechanism.
